source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substring including written/read and other annotations.
source.public_versification_note: Exact XML records mapped to public labels; Zechariah 1:18–2:13 and Malachi 4 have different Hebrew chapter boundaries.

delta_method: F0 retained; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential choices flagged by the selective apparatus. Classification remains provisional. Overlap is triage only, with no change quota.

comparative_references.scope: Programmatic alignment after recovery of unfinished original-language drafts; selected bilingual rereads recorded separately. TSW is not the base text.

verses.rationale: Retains the vision verb and prophetic oracle label.
verses.before: The oracle that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
verses.after: The oracle that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
verses.tsw_comparator: The oracle that Habakkuk the prophet saw.

verses.rationale: Makes the complaint audible without resolving its accusation against divine inaction.
verses.before: How long, O LORD, will I cry for help, and you do not hear? I cry to you, “Violence!” and you do not save.
verses.after: How long, LORD, must I cry for help while you do not listen? I cry out to you, “Violence!” but you do not save.
verses.tsw_comparator: How long, O LORD, shall I cry for help, and you do not hear? I cry to you, “Violence!” and you do not save.

verses.rationale: Preserves the change from the prophet seeing to God looking and the escalating conflict.
verses.before: Why do you make me see iniquity, and why do you look upon trouble? Destruction and violence are before me; strife arises, and contention lifts itself up.
verses.after: Why do you make me see wrongdoing and look on at misery? Destruction and violence confront me; strife breaks out and conflict rises.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you make me see iniquity, and why do you look upon trouble? Destruction and violence are before me; strife arises, and contention lifts itself up.

verses.rationale: Connects the repeated consequence while retaining instruction and distorted justice.
verses.before: So instruction grows numb, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked surrounds the righteous; so justice goes forth twisted.
verses.after: So instruction is paralyzed, and justice never prevails. The wicked surround the righteous; that is why justice comes out twisted.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore instruction grows numb, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked surrounds the righteous; therefore justice goes forth twisted.

verses.rationale: Keeps the plural summons and the work’s initially unexpressed agent.
verses.before: Look among the nations and see; be astonished—be amazed. For I am working a work in your days that you would not trust if it were told.
verses.after: “Look among the nations! Look closely! Be utterly astonished! For a work is being done in your days that you would not believe if told.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look among the nations and see; be astonished—be amazed. For I am working a work in your days that you would not trust if it were told.

verses.rationale: Retains Chaldeans and the concrete seizure of others’ homes.
verses.before: For look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, who march through the breadth of the earth to possess dwelling places that are not theirs.
verses.after: I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter, headlong nation, who march across the breadth of the earth to seize homes that are not theirs.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, who march through the breadth of the earth to possess dwelling places that are not theirs.

verses.rationale: Keeps the accusation of self-authorized rule without supplying modern political labels.
verses.before: They are terrifying and fearsome; their judgment and their dignity come from themselves.
verses.after: They are frightening and fearsome; their justice and authority come from themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are terrifying and fearsome; their judgment and their dignity come from themselves.

verses.rationale: Retains both horsemen clauses and the predator images.
verses.before: Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves of evening. Their horsemen spring forward; their horsemen come from far away. They fly like an eagle hastening to devour.
verses.after: Their horses are faster than leopards, fiercer than wolves at dusk. Their horsemen spread out; their horsemen come from far away, flying like an eagle rushing to feed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves of evening. Their horsemen spring forward; their horsemen come from far away. They fly like an eagle hastening to devour.

verses.rationale: Follows the difficult eastward wording provisionally and preserves the innumerable captives image.
verses.before: All of them come for violence; the direction of their faces is forward. They gather captives like sand.
verses.after: They all come for violence, their faces pressing eastward. They gather captives like sand.
verses.tsw_comparator: All of them come for violence; the direction of their faces is forward. They gather captives like sand.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated laughter and the concrete siege-ramp action.
verses.before: They mock kings, and rulers are a joke to them. They laugh at every fortress; they heap up earth and capture it.
verses.after: They mock kings and laugh at rulers. They laugh at every fortress, heap up earth, and capture it.
verses.tsw_comparator: They mock kings, and rulers are a joke to them. They laugh at every fortress; they heap up earth and capture it.

verses.rationale: Takes wind as comparison and keeps guilt attached to the invader’s self-deification.
verses.before: Then they sweep by like wind and pass on. They become guilty— this strength of theirs is their god.
verses.after: Then they sweep on like the wind and pass through— guilty people, whose strength is their god.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they sweep by like wind and pass on. They become guilty— this strength of theirs is their god.

verses.rationale: Keeps the pinned we-will-not-die reading and both divine titles.
verses.before: Are you not from everlasting, O LORD my God, my Holy One? We will not die. O LORD, you appointed them for judgment; O Rock, you established them for correction.
verses.after: Are you not from ancient times, LORD my God, my Holy One? We will not die. LORD, you appointed them for judgment; Rock, you established them for correction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Are you not from everlasting, O LORD my God, my Holy One? We shall not die. O LORD, you appointed them for judgment; O Rock, you established them for correction.

verses.rationale: Preserves the deliberate tension between inability to look and looking on.
verses.before: Your eyes are too pure to look upon evil, and you cannot gaze upon trouble. Why do you gaze upon people who act treacherously? Why are you silent when the wicked swallows one more righteous than himself?
verses.after: Your eyes are too pure to look on evil; you cannot gaze at misery. Why, then, do you look on at traitors and stay silent when the wicked swallow those more righteous than themselves?
verses.tsw_comparator: Your eyes are too pure to look upon evil, and you cannot gaze upon trouble. Why do you gaze upon those who act treacherously? Why are you silent when the wicked swallows one more righteous than himself?

verses.rationale: Retains God as grammatical agent and human vulnerability in the animal comparison.
verses.before: You make humanity like the fish of the sea, like crawling things that have no ruler.
verses.after: You make human beings like fish in the sea, like crawling creatures with no ruler.
verses.tsw_comparator: You make humanity like the fish of the sea, like crawling things that have no ruler.

verses.rationale: Identifies the continuing hostile singular figure for readers and retains all fishing implements.
verses.before: He brings all of them up with a hook; he drags them away with his net and gathers them in his dragnet. So he rejoices and is glad.
verses.after: The enemy hauls them all up with a hook, drags them in his net, gathers them in his dragnet. That is why he rejoices and celebrates.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brings all of them up with a hook; he drags them away with his net and gathers them in his dragnet. Therefore he rejoices and is glad.

verses.rationale: Connects idolatrous worship to material benefit without turning the metaphor into explanation.
verses.before: So he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet, for by them his portion is rich and his food is abundant.
verses.after: That is why he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet: through them his share is rich and his food plentiful.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet, for by them his portion is rich and his food is abundant.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unresolved closing question and repeated predation.
verses.before: Will he therefore keep emptying his net and continually killing nations without compassion?
verses.after: Will he keep emptying his net, then, and killing nations without mercy?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will he therefore keep emptying his net and continually killing nations without compassion?

verses.rationale: Retains first-person answer rather than changing it to God’s answer; notes the final clause’s difficulty.
verses.before: I will stand at my watchpost and station myself on the rampart. I will watch to see what he will speak to me and what I will answer concerning my complaint.
verses.after: I will stand at my watchpost and take my place on the rampart. I will watch to see what he says to me and how I should answer about my complaint.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will stand at my watchpost and station myself on the rampart. I will watch to see what he will speak to me and what I will answer concerning my complaint.

verses.rationale: Keeps the running reader image without choosing reading-on-the-run or messenger exclusively.
verses.before: Then the LORD answered me and said: “Write the vision; make it plain on tablets, so that the one who reads it may run.
verses.after: The LORD answered me: “Write the vision; make it plain on tablets, so the one who reads it can run.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD answered me and said: “Write the vision; make it plain on tablets, so that the one who reads it may run.

verses.rationale: Retains the deliberate delay/not-late tension and the certain coming.
verses.before: For the vision is still for the appointed time; it breathes toward the end and will not lie. Though it delays, wait for it, for it will surely come; it will not be late.
verses.after: The vision is still for its appointed time. It presses toward the end and will not lie. If it delays, wait for it; it will surely come. It will not be late.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the vision is still for the appointed time; it breathes toward the end and will not lie. Though it delays, wait for it, for it will surely come; it will not be late.

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult swollen description and personal faithfulness, with faith’s range noted.
verses.before: Look, his life is puffed up; it is not upright within him, but the righteous will live by his faithfulness.
verses.after: Look at the swollen one— his life within him is not upright. But the righteous will live by their faithfulness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, his life is puffed up; it is not upright within him, but the righteous will live by his faithfulness.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned wine rather than an emendation and retains Sheol and insatiable conquest.
verses.before: Indeed, wine betrays; the arrogant man does not rest. He enlarges his appetite like Sheol, and like death he is never satisfied. He gathers to himself all the nations and collects to himself all the peoples.
verses.after: Wine, too, betrays. The arrogant man will not stay at rest. He opens his appetite as wide as Sheol; like death, he is never satisfied. He gathers all nations to himself and collects all peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, wine betrays; the arrogant man does not rest. He enlarges his appetite like Sheol, and like death he is never satisfied. He gathers to himself all the nations and collects to himself all the peoples.

verses.rationale: Keeps the embedded how-long cry and ambiguous debt/pledge image.
verses.before: Will not all these take up a taunt against him, a mocking riddle concerning him, and say: “Woe to the one who multiplies what is not his— for how long?— and loads himself with pledges!
verses.after: Will not all of them take up a taunt against him, a mocking riddle, and say: ‘Woe to the one who piles up what is not his— how long?— and loads himself with pledges!’
verses.tsw_comparator: Will not all these take up a taunt against him, a mocking riddle concerning him, and say: “Woe to the one who multiplies what is not his— for how long?— and loads himself with pledges!

verses.rationale: Retains the reversal and notes the biting/creditor wordplay.
verses.before: Will not your creditors suddenly rise, and people who make you tremble awaken? Then you will become plunder for them.
verses.after: Will not your creditors suddenly rise? Will not those who make you tremble wake up? Then you will become their plunder.
verses.tsw_comparator: Will not your creditors suddenly rise, and those who make you tremble awaken? Then you will become plunder for them.

verses.rationale: Maintains repeated plunder and the full refrain of harmed places and people.
verses.before: Because you plundered many nations, all the remnant of the peoples will plunder you, because of human blood and violence against the land, the city, and everyone who live in it.
verses.after: Because you plundered many nations, all the peoples left will plunder you— for human bloodshed and violence against the land, the city, and all who live in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because you plundered many nations, all the remnant of the peoples will plunder you, because of human blood and violence against the land, the city, and all who live in it.

verses.rationale: Keeps house/nest relation and the ironic attempt to secure safety through harm.
verses.before: Woe to the one who gains evil gain for his house, setting his nest on high to be delivered from the hand of disaster!
verses.after: Woe to the one who makes evil profit for his house, setting his nest high to escape the reach of harm!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to the one who gains evil gain for his house, setting his nest on high to be delivered from the hand of disaster!

verses.rationale: Retains the reflexive cost of the oppressor’s plan.
verses.before: You have counseled shame for your house, cutting off many peoples, and you have sinned against your own life.
verses.after: You have planned shame for your own house by cutting off many peoples; you have sinned against your own life.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have counseled shame for your house, cutting off many peoples, and you have sinned against your own life.

verses.rationale: Preserves the building materials as speaking witnesses.
verses.before: For a stone from the wall will cry out, and a beam from the woodwork will answer it.
verses.after: A stone will cry out from the wall, and a timber beam will answer it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a stone from the wall will cry out, and a beam from the woodwork will answer it.

verses.rationale: Keeps both building clauses and distinct bloodshed/injustice terms.
verses.before: Woe to the one who builds a city with blood and establishes a town with injustice!
verses.after: Woe to the one who builds a town with bloodshed and establishes a city through injustice!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to the one who builds a city with blood and establishes a town with injustice!

verses.rationale: Makes the rhetorical question readable while retaining the destruction of labor’s results.
verses.before: Look, is it not from the LORD of Hosts that peoples labor only for fire and nations weary themselves for emptiness?
verses.after: Is this not from the LORD of Armies: peoples labor only to feed the fire, and nations exhaust themselves for nothing?
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, is it not from the LORD of Hosts that peoples labor only for fire and nations weary themselves for emptiness?

verses.rationale: Retains the recognizable image and glory rather than forcing novelty.
verses.before: For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
verses.after: For the earth will be filled with knowledge of the LORD’s glory, as waters cover the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.

verses.rationale: Preserves the source’s person shifts and sexual exposure; notes fury/poison ambiguity.
verses.before: Woe to the one who makes his neighbor drink, pouring out your wrath and making them drunk in order to gaze upon their nakedness!
verses.after: Woe to the one who makes his neighbor drink, pouring out your fury and making them drunk so you can look at their nakedness!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to the one who makes his neighbor drink, pouring out your wrath and making them drunk in order to gaze upon their nakedness!

verses.rationale: Retains the pinned uncircumcision image and the shame/glory reversal.
verses.before: You are filled with shame instead of glory. Drink—you also— and expose your uncircumcision! The cup in the LORD’s right hand will come around to you, and disgrace will cover your glory.
verses.after: You are filled with disgrace instead of glory. Drink, you too, and expose your uncircumcision! The cup in the LORD’s right hand will come around to you, and filthy shame will cover your glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are filled with shame instead of glory. Drink—you also— and expose your uncircumcision! The cup in the LORD’s right hand will come around to you, and disgrace will cover your glory.

verses.rationale: Restores a readable parallel clause while retaining the difficult animals/them pronoun and the explicit cause.
verses.before: For the violence done to Lebanon will cover you, and the destruction of animals will terrify you, because of human blood and violence against the land, the city, and everyone who live in it.
verses.after: For the violence done to Lebanon will engulf you, as will the destruction of animals that terrified them, because of human bloodshed and violence against the land, the city, and all who live in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the violence done to Lebanon will cover you, and the destruction of animals will terrify you, because of human blood and violence against the land, the city, and all who live in it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the maker/made recurrence and mute idols in natural syntax.
verses.before: What profit is a carved image when its maker has carved it, a cast image and a teacher of falsehood? For its maker trusts in what he has made when he makes speechless idols.
verses.after: What use is a carved image that its maker carved, a cast image that teaches lies? Its maker trusts his own creation, making idols that cannot speak.
verses.tsw_comparator: What profit is a carved image when its maker has carved it, a cast image and a teacher of falsehood? For its maker trusts in what he has made when he makes speechless idols.

verses.rationale: Retains direct absurd commands and the contrast of costly covering and absent breath.
verses.before: Woe to the one who says to wood, “Wake up!” to silent stone, “Rise!” Can it teach? Look, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all within it.
verses.after: Woe to the one who tells wood, ‘Wake up!’ and a silent stone, ‘Get up!’ Can it teach? Look, it is coated with gold and silver, but there is no breath at all inside it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to the one who says to wood, “Wake up!” to silent stone, “Rise!” Can it teach? Look, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all within it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrast with mute idols and universal silence.
verses.before: But the LORD is in his holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before him.
verses.after: But the LORD is in his holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD is in his holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the uncertain performance term rather than inventing a musical description.
verses.before: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, according to Shigionoth.
verses.after: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, according to Shigionoth.
verses.tsw_comparator: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, according to Shigionoth.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated years and the appeal for compassion within divine upheaval.
verses.before: O LORD, I have heard your report; I fear. O LORD, revive your work among the years; among the years make it known. In wrath, remember compassion.
verses.after: LORD, I have heard the report about you; I am afraid. LORD, bring your work to life in these years; make it known in these years. In your turmoil, remember compassion.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, I have heard your report; I fear. O LORD, revive your work in the midst of the years; in the midst of the years make it known. In wrath, remember compassion.

verses.rationale: Preserves locations, the divine appearance, and the performance marker.
verses.before: God comes from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His splendor covers the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise.
verses.after: God comes from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His splendor covers the heavens; his praise fills the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: God comes from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His splendor covers the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise.

verses.rationale: Renders horns as rays in the light context and notes the literal image.
verses.before: His brightness is like the light; rays flash from his hand, and there his power is hidden.
verses.after: His brightness is like light; rays flash from his hand, and there his power is hidden.
verses.tsw_comparator: His brightness is like the light; rays flash from his hand, and there his power is hidden.

verses.rationale: Retains the personified attendants without adding mythological identities.
verses.before: Plague goes before him, and pestilence goes out at his feet.
verses.after: Plague goes before him, and pestilence follows at his feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: Plague goes before him, and pestilence goes out at his feet.

verses.rationale: Follows measures rather than silently changing the verb to shakes; preserves ancient/everlasting contrasts.
verses.before: He stands and shakes the earth; he looks and makes the nations tremble. The everlasting mountains are shattered; the ancient hills sink down. His are the ways of eternity.
verses.after: He stands and measures the earth; he looks, and nations leap in alarm. Ancient mountains shatter; age-old hills bow down. His paths are everlasting.
verses.tsw_comparator: He stands and shakes the earth; he looks and makes the nations tremble. The everlasting mountains are shattered; the ancient hills sink down. His are the ways of eternity.

verses.rationale: Retains Cushan as written and the parallel tent images.
verses.before: Under trouble I see the tents of Cushan; the curtains of the land of Midian tremble.
verses.after: I see the tents of Cushan under affliction; the tent curtains of Midian tremble.
verses.tsw_comparator: Under trouble I see the tents of Cushan; the curtains of the land of Midian tremble.

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift into direct address and the repeated question rather than explaining it away.
verses.before: Was your anger against the rivers, O LORD? Was your anger against the rivers, or your wrath against the sea, when you rode upon your horses, upon your chariots of salvation?
verses.after: Was the LORD angry with the rivers? Was your anger against the rivers, your fury against the sea, when you rode your horses, your chariots of salvation?
verses.tsw_comparator: Was your anger against the rivers, O LORD? Was your anger against the rivers, or your wrath against the sea, when you rode upon your horses, upon your chariots of salvation?

verses.rationale: Preserves the very uncertain middle words in a restrained rendering with an explicit note, not a confident invented scene.
verses.before: You uncovered your bow; sworn were the shafts of your word. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.
verses.after: You draw your bow bare— oaths, rods, a word. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.
verses.tsw_comparator: You uncovered your bow; sworn were the shafts of your word. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.

verses.rationale: Keeps the natural world’s bodily personification.
verses.before: The mountains see you and writhe. A torrent of waters passes by; the deep gives its voice and lifts its hands on high.
verses.after: The mountains see you and writhe; a torrent of water sweeps past. The deep raises its voice and lifts its hands high.
verses.tsw_comparator: The mountains see you and writhe. A torrent of waters passes by; the deep gives its voice and lifts its hands on high.

verses.rationale: Retains celestial stillness and both divine weapons.
verses.before: Sun and moon stand in their lofty place at the light of your arrows as they go, at the brightness of the lightning of your spear.
verses.after: Sun and moon stand still in their dwelling at the light of your flying arrows, at the gleam of your flashing spear.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sun and moon stand in their lofty place at the light of your arrows as they go, at the brightness of the lightning of your spear.

verses.rationale: Keeps the agricultural violence image and parallel emotions.
verses.before: In indignation you march through the earth; in anger you thresh the nations.
verses.after: In indignation you march through the earth; in anger you thresh the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: In indignation you march through the earth; in anger you thresh the nations.

verses.rationale: Retains the unnamed anointed one and mixed house/body image without harmonizing it.
verses.before: You went out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of your anointed. You crushed the head from the house of the wicked, laying bare the foundation to the neck. Selah.
verses.after: You go out to save your people, to save your anointed one. You crush the head of the wicked house, laying it bare from foundation to neck. Selah.
verses.tsw_comparator: You went out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of your anointed. You crushed the head from the house of the wicked, laying bare the foundation to the neck. Selah.

verses.rationale: Follows the read plural warriors and preserves me and the predatory comparison.
verses.before: You pierced the head of his warriors with his own shafts. They stormed out to scatter me; their exultation was as if to devour the poor in secret.
verses.after: With his own shafts you pierce the head of his warriors, who storm out to scatter me, delighting as though to devour the poor in hiding.
verses.tsw_comparator: You pierced the head of his warriors with his own shafts. They stormed out to scatter me; their exultation was as if to devour the poor in secret.

verses.rationale: Retains the mounted divine action and turbulent waters.
verses.before: You trod the sea with your horses, the churning of mighty waters.
verses.after: You tread through the sea with your horses, through the surge of mighty waters.
verses.tsw_comparator: You trod the sea with your horses, the churning of mighty waters.

verses.rationale: Unfolds bodily fear into readable clauses and records the difficult final expectation without overclaiming certainty.
verses.before: I hear, and my inward parts tremble; at the sound my lips quiver. Decay enters my bones, and beneath me I tremble. Yet I wait quietly for the day of distress to come upon the people who attack us.
verses.after: I hear, and my body trembles; at the sound my lips quiver. Decay enters my bones, and my legs shake beneath me. Yet I will wait quietly for the day of distress to come upon the people who raid us.
verses.tsw_comparator: I hear, and my inward parts tremble; at the sound my lips quiver. Decay enters my bones, and beneath me I tremble. Yet I wait quietly for the day of distress to come upon the people who attack us.

verses.rationale: Keeps all six losses and lets the concessive sentence continue into the next verse.
verses.before: Though the fig tree does not blossom, and there is no fruit on the vines; though the produce of the olive fails, and the fields yield no food; though the flock is cut off from the fold, and there are no cattle in the stalls—
verses.after: Though the fig tree does not blossom and there is no fruit on the vines, though the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, though the flock is cut off from the pen and there are no cattle in the stalls,
verses.tsw_comparator: Though the fig tree does not blossom, and there is no fruit on the vines; though the produce of the olive fails, and the fields yield no food; though the flock is cut off from the fold, and there are no cattle in the stalls—

verses.rationale: Retains the first-person resolve and double rejoicing despite the preceding losses.
verses.before: yet I will rejoice in the LORD; I will exult in the God of my salvation.
verses.after: yet I will celebrate in the LORD; I will rejoice in the God who saves me.
verses.tsw_comparator: yet I will rejoice in the LORD; I will exult in the God of my salvation.

verses.rationale: Preserves both divine designations, personal heights, and the final performance direction inside its verse.
verses.before: The LORD, my Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like the feet of a deer and makes me tread upon my heights. To the director, with my stringed instruments.
verses.after: The LORD, the Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like a deer’s and leads me on my heights. For the music leader, with my stringed instruments.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD, my Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like the feet of a deer and makes me tread upon my heights. To the director, with my stringed instruments.
